notes.text: Wide freezing range (~120 K) makes sterling mushy-freezing and prone to shrinkage porosity; feed heavy sections directly.
Firescale = internal Cu oxide; Cu-free/Pd-containing 925 alloys avoid it. Deoxidised grains (Si, Zn) reduce gas porosity and firescale.
Si additions increase fluidity but widen melting range (dT ~150-170 C) and raise shrinkage porosity susceptibility; keep flask <=500-540 C for Si alloys; limit scrap to <=50%.
Si >=0.1% markedly raises hot-tearing susceptibility; Zn raises it less; grain refiners nearly eliminate it.
Zn lowers surface tension and improves form filling but evaporates during melting (high vapour pressure).

rules.locator: Rule 2 'Diameter should be greater than the thickness of the pattern attached'

rules.statement: Sprue at least 25% larger than the heaviest portion of the piece; add a sprue for higher karats.
Ingate cross-section ~1:1 with the section of the piece at the attachment.

alt.locator: 'cross sectional area of the feed sprue should be between 70 and 150%' of attachment point, depending on authority
gate >= 2/3 of cross-sectional area of the thick wall

rules.statement: Do not use choke (necked) gates; they cut off feed metal. Flare the gate where it meets the piece.
Keep feed sprues short: max ~3/4 in (19 mm); if longer, increase diameter.
Attach feed sprues at ~45 deg to the main sprue (smallest pieces top, largest bottom).

alt.locator: vacuum casting: 'more like a T than a Y, ~80 degrees'
Pt centrifugal: parts under 90 deg to main sprue give less turbulence
p.310/316 waxes at almost right angle to sprue (Pt)

rules.conflict: 45 deg (Stuller) vs 80-90 deg (H&S vacuum, Progold, Pt simulation)

rules.statement: Taper sprues ~1.1:1 (straight) and ~1.3:1 (bent) to reduce turbulence.
rules.locator: 'ratio of 1.1:1 for straight sprues and 1.3:1 for bent sprues'

rules.statement: Use round sprue sections: a round 3 mm tube passed ~45% more fluid than a flattened one, and round sections freeze later.

alt.locator: p.6 rounded sections for fluid- and thermodynamic reasons

rules.statement: The central (main) sprue must act as reservoir and be the last part of the tree to solidify; give it adequate volume.
Reservoirs/tanks: spherical, with a very short ingate.
Solidification time t = B (V/A)^n, n ~= 2 (Askeland); 1.5-2 (Degarmo). Modulus M = V/A.
Feeder (sprue/button) solidification time should exceed the casting's by ~25%.
rules.locator: '25% longer is usually a safe choice'

alt.locator: risers solidification time e.g. 25% longer than casting

rules.statement: Feeder modulus >= ~1.12 x modulus of the section fed (from t-ratio 1.25 with n=2).
rules.method: sqrt(1.25) combining feeder_time_ratio with chvorinov n=2

rules.statement: No published Chvorinov mould constant B for gypsum-bonded jewellery investment was found; B must be calibrated (e.g., by simulation/experiment).
rules.locator: investment thermal conductivity could not be determined from literature; measured and used to calibrate simulation

rules.statement: A hot spot forms where heavy sprues join the ring; a ring shank can act as feeder for a thick section and leave centreline pores - feed thick sections directly.
In tilt casting (Pt) reducing main sprue diameter from 10 to 5 mm increased filling speed and saved ~50% tree weight.
No feeding uphill in thicker sections (adverse pressure gradient, convection).
Keep liquid metal meniscus velocity below ~0.5 m/s to avoid surface-film entrainment.
Leave ~10 mm between pieces on the tree and 10-15 mm at the sprue extremity.
Keep >=7 mm investment between wax and flask wall (Pt).
Platinum: short, thicker sprues than for gold/silver, oriented to the centrifugal force direction.
Superheat above liquidus / flask temperature by piece size: large +30C/482C, medium +60C/538C, small/intricate +100C/593C.
Karat gold: vacuum-assist pour 100-200F (56-111C) over melt temperature; centrifugal 50-125F (28-69C) over.
Gypsum investment (Satin Cast 20) flask: filigree/ladies rings 482-538C; heavy gents rings 371-482C; max burnout 732C.
Volume shrinkage on solidification of most metals: 3-7%; most Ag and Au alloys 5-6%.

CaSO4 in gypsum-bonded investment decomposes to CaO + SO2 between ~900 and 1260C; melt/investment reaction is a primary cause of gas porosity. Use phosphate/silica Pt investments for Pt, Pd and high-melting alloys.
